questions.question: Alcohol impairs your riding ability:

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your riding skills.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Is too warm to wear while riding.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a leather jacket when riding for protection. In hot weather, leather jackets are designed to keep you cool and prevent dehydration.

questions.question: If another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: Get a tailgater ahead of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes tailgating more dangerous at higher speeds.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours that have passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours means about four drinks remain in the body.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders can use three different positions within their lane. Choose the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and never use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast causes the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet because it might cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly on rough surfaces to keep control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply both brakes together at the same time.

questions.question: How can other drivers see you better at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight while riding.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight while riding.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see it best. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can react to dangers. Eye contact alone is not enough to ensure drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your chance of crashing, be visible to other drivers. Tell them what you plan to do. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look at least 12 seconds ahead. Notice hazards early. Be ready for changes.

questions.question: When riding at night instead of during the day, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow other vehicles closely.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of other vehicles to see farther ahead. Be flexible about your lane position at night.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Done safely by using only the front brake.
Done safely by using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black words or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make the motorcycle more unstable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To reduce your crash risk, be as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks must a rider have before feeling alcohol's effects?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A snug-fitting baseball cap
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Which formation keeps motorcycle group riders closest together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while allowing each rider enough space. Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver can see you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Skip using your turn signals when changing lanes.
Only watch about five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid a sudden hazard.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a sidecar passenger affects how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes to let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the manufacturer's recommended settings for that weight.
